def same_label(a: str | None, b: str | None) -> bool:
    """
    Revision or requirement labels as different records write them: "Rev. C", "Revision C" and "C" are equal,
    "REQ-01" and "Req 1" too; label words (rev, revision, anforderung, ...) and separators do not count, every
    other letter and number does ("Rev. B" is not "C", "C-1" is not "C"). A document number around the revision word
    and a date in brackets do not count ("DOC-12 Revision C (26.9.)" is "C").
    """
    ta, tb = _label_tokens(a), _label_tokens(b)
    return bool(ta) and ta == tb

async def specification(self, site: str, erp_site: str | None) -> None:
        """
        The specification, twice at once: a fast navigator (thinking off) and a careful one (thinking on, more
        steps) work in separate contexts of the website; the first that yields a revision with requirements wins
        and the other is cancelled. Requirements stream to the ERP as soon as either attempt reads them, all from
        one revision (the first one read); requirements read before an attempt stopped are kept.
        """
        board = self.board
        erp = None
        if erp_site:
            if self._erp is None:
                self._erp = Erp(self.access[erp_site], self.contexts[erp_site], self.trace, self.research_deadline)
                self._erp.warm_up()
            erp = self._erp
        spare = None
        try:
            context = self.task["brief"].split("## Rules")[0].strip()
            spare = await self._spare_context(site)
            attempts = {
                asyncio.create_task(self._spec_attempt(site, "spec", self.contexts[site], context, erp,
                                                       thinking=False, steps=SPEC_STEPS_FAST)): "fast",
                asyncio.create_task(self._spec_attempt(site, "spec2", spare or self.contexts[site], context, erp,
                                                       thinking=True, steps=SPEC_STEPS_THINKING)): "thinking",
            }
            results: list[SpecResult] = []
            pending = set(attempts)
            while pending and self.spec is None:
                done, pending = await asyncio.wait(pending, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
                for task in done:
                    if task.cancelled() or task.exception() is not None:
                        error = None if task.cancelled() else task.exception()
                        board.problem("specification", f"{attempts[task]} attempt failed: {type(error).__name__}: "
                                                       f"{str(error)[:160]}")
                        continue
                    result = task.result()
                    results.append(result)
                    if result.current_revision and result.requirements and self.spec is None:
                        self.spec = result
                        self.trace.event("specification", "winner", attempt=attempts[task],
                                         revision=result.current_revision, seconds=result.seconds)
                    else:
                        for problem in result.problems:
                            board.problem("specification", f"{attempts[task]} attempt: {problem}")
            for task in pending:  # the other attempt is no longer needed
                task.cancel()
            if pending:
                await asyncio.gather(*pending, return_exceptions=True)
            await self._close_context(spare)  # its tabs would compete with the ERP workers for the browser
            spare = None
            if self.spec is None:  # neither finished with requirements: keep the most that was read
                self.spec = max(results, key=lambda r: len(r.requirements), default=SpecResult())
            self._adopt_revision(self.spec, site, erp)
            for problem in self.spec.problems:
                board.problem("specification", problem)
            if not self.requirements:
                board.problem("specification", "no requirement read")
            if erp is None:
                return
            self.erp = await erp.collect()
            await self._post_materials(erp_site or "")
        except Exception as error:
            board.problem("specification", f"{type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:200]}")
        finally:
            board.finish("requirement")
            board.finish("material")
            await self._close_context(spare)

    async def _close_context(context: BrowserContext | None) -> None:

async def _early_no_bid(self) -> None:
        """
        Tender, specification and ERP research are done while the mail searches still run. When the answer is a
        no_bid on established evidence (a position has no matching active material after the final choice, the
        Q&A re-check and the wording check, all run here as _answer would run them), the mail searches that only
        price positions are ended: a no_bid answer needs none of them, only the discount approval (rule 16). In the
        err404-nobid eval a no_bid waited about nine minutes for mail kinds it never used. Anything that turns the
        decision back into a bid leaves the mail searches running.
        """
        result = self._calculate()[0]
        if result is None or result.decision != "no_bid" or not result.missing_materials:
            return
        self.trace.event("verify", "no_bid_early", missing=result.missing_materials, seconds_left=round(self.left()))
        await self._bounded(self.select_materials(), "select")
        result = self._calculate()[0]
        if result is None or result.decision != "no_bid" or not result.missing_materials:
            return
        again = await self.recheck_no_bid(result.missing_materials)
        self.no_bid_rechecked = True
        if again is not None and again[0] is not None:
            result = again[0]
            if result.decision != "no_bid" or not result.missing_materials:
                self.trace.event("verify", "no_bid_overturned", by="Q&A re-check", early=True)
                return
        try:
            rescued = await asyncio.wait_for(self.wording_matches(result.missing_materials),
                                             max(1.0, min(VERIFY_SECONDS, self.form_left() - 30)))
        except Exception as error:
            rescued = {}
            self.board.problem("verify", f"wording check: {type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:160]}")
        if rescued:
            self.chosen = {**self.chosen, **rescued}
            again = self._calculate()
            if again[0] is not None and again[0].decision == "bid":
                self.trace.event("verify", "no_bid_overturned", chosen=rescued, early=True)
                return
        self.no_bid_settled = list(result.missing_materials)
        await self._cut_mail(NO_BID_KEEP)

    async def _cut_mail(self, keep: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
        """End the mail searches once the kinds in `keep` have been searched (or NO_BID_MAIL_WAIT has passed);
        what was read so far is resolved as at the mail deadline."""
        wanted = {k.name for k in self.mail_kinds if k.name in keep}
        until = min(self.mail_deadline, time.monotonic() + NO_BID_MAIL_WAIT)
        while (wanted - set(self.mail_results) and time.monotonic() < until
               and any(not t.done() for t in self._mail_tabs)):
            await asyncio.sleep(1.0)
        if not self.mail_kinds:  # not planned yet: nothing known to cut
            return
        cut = [t for t in self._mail_tabs if not t.done()]
        for task in cut:
            task.cancel()
        self.trace.event("mails", "cut", reason="no_bid settled", tabs=len(cut),
                         read=sorted(self.mail_results), dropped=sorted({k.name for k in self.mail_kinds}
                                                                        - set(self.mail_results)))

    def _finished_erp(self) -> ErpResearch:

def idents(found):
    return {g.ident: g.positions for g in found}


class DetectGaps(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_implausible_base_price_rereads_fx(self):
        o = state([position("1", "A-1")], [requirement("A-1")],
                  [RequirementResearch(requirement_id="A-1", inspected=["M-1"], selected="M-1")],
                  {"M-1": complete_record("M-1")})
        problem = "position 1: base price 55000.00 EUR is 1.1e+04 x the ERP scale price 5 USD per piece (FX rate " \
                  "11000 implausible); field left blank"
        self.assertEqual(idents(detect_gaps(o, [problem])), {"mail/fx": ("1",)})

    def test_complete_answer_has_no_gaps(self):
        o = state([position("1", "A-1")], [requirement("A-1")],
                  [RequirementResearch(requirement_id="A-1", inspected=["M-1"], selected="M-1")],
                  {"M-1": complete_record("M-1")})
        self.assertEqual(detect_gaps(o), [])

    def test_each_reason_for_an_omitted_position(self):
        o = state([position("1", "A-1"), position("2", "A-2"), position("3", "A-3"), position("4", "A-4"),
                   position("5", "A-5"), position("6", "A-6")],
                  [requirement("A-2"), requirement("A-3"), requirement("A-4", "K-9"), requirement("A-5"),
                   requirement("A-6")],
                  [RequirementResearch(requirement_id="A-2", problems=["search worker returned no result"]),
                   RequirementResearch(requirement_id="A-3", inspected=["M-3"], problems=["no valid choice"]),
                   RequirementResearch(requirement_id="A-4", inspected=["M-4"], problems=["stroke pending"]),
                   RequirementResearch(requirement_id="A-5", inspected=["M-5"]),  # complete search, no match
                   RequirementResearch(requirement_id="A-6", inspected=["M-6"], selected="M-6")])
        self.assertEqual(idents(detect_gaps(o)), {
            "requirement/A-1": ("1",), "erp/A-2": ("2",), "erp/A-3": ("3",), "mail/end_reserves": ("4",),
            "material/M-6": ("6",)})

    def test_an_empty_catalogue_group_is_no_gap(self):
        research = RequirementResearch(requirement_id="A-1")
        if "no_hits" not in RequirementResearch.model_fields:
            self.skipTest("no no_hits field")
        research.no_hits = True
        o = state([position("1", "A-1")], [requirement("A-1")], [research])
        self.assertEqual(detect_gaps(o), [])

    def test_unresolved_keys_and_calc_problems_name_their_mail_kind(self):
        o = state([position("1", "A-1", packaging_key="P-1", condition_group="K-1"),
                   position("2", "A-1", packaging_key="P-1", bonus_key="B-1")],
                  [requirement("A-1")],
                  [RequirementResearch(requirement_id="A-1", inspected=["M-1"], selected="M-1")],
                  {"M-1": complete_record("M-1")}, mail=mail_facts(approval=None, discount_scopes={"K-1": "x"}))
        found = idents(detect_gaps(o, ["position 2 omitted: no FX rate for USD",
                                       "position 1: no metal index rate valid on 2026-06-01; field left blank"]))
        self.assertEqual(found, {"mail/approval": (), "mail/packaging": ("1", "2"), "mail/project_bonus": ("2",),
                                 "mail/fx": ("2",), "mail/metal_indices": ("1",)})

    def test_irrelevant_missing_material_facts_are_no_gap(self):
        record = complete_record("M-1").model_copy(update={"pieces_per_carton": None, "allocation_mass_kg": None})
        o = state([position("1", "A-1")], [requirement("A-1")],
                  [RequirementResearch(requirement_id="A-1", inspected=["M-1"], selected="M-1")], {"M-1": record})
        self.assertEqual(detect_gaps(o), [])
        o.tender_facts.positions = [position("1", "A-1", packaging_key="P-1")]
        o.mail_facts.packaging = {"P-1": object()}
        self.assertEqual(idents(detect_gaps(o)), {"material/M-1": ("1",)})

Two more bugs from our layout eval `err404-layout` (`ev_a9a0e35856f48112`). Main scored 46.9 there twice, and 100 locally. Its README and DERIVATION are in `evals/err404-layout/` on main.

1. **The Q&A on a different site is never read.** This causes all of main's losses on that eval.
   - The planner treats "tender" as one fact kind covering both the positions and the Q&A (`orchestrator.py:90-93`). On the platform it assigned that kind only to the tender site, but the Q&A lives on the spec site (`buyer-extranet`). The Q&A reader found nothing (`qa_incomplete collected=0`), and the re-checks only revisit the planned sites (`orchestrator.py:~1104-1131`).
   - Fix: make the Q&A its own fact kind in `FACT_KINDS` so the planner places it separately. Also, when a Q&A read on a site returns nothing, try the other non-mail sites, the spec site first.
   - This fits your tender/Q&A scope.
2. **The TAN lookup is slow on a different mailbox** (`submit.py`):
   - The goal text (`tan_goal` ~121-130) only says "TAN", but the mail says "signing code".
   - `TAN_STEPS` is 16.
   - Line ~679 tells the model to request a new TAN after any failed lookup, so it requested 9 codes. Each new one goes to the last page of an oldest-first list.
   - Fix: describe it as "TAN / one-time signing or confirmation code", note that lists may be oldest first (go to the last page or search), retry the lookup for the same code before requesting a new one, and raise `TAN_STEPS` to about 24.
3. **Submission-only issue:** when every position is omitted but the checker says no_bid, follow no_bid (rule 9). Check that main does this.

Include err404-layout in your eval runs: at most 3 eval runs in total, because of the hourly limit.

            on_facts(early)
        try:

        except Exception as error:

    finally:
        if not qa_task.done():

def _finish(session: SiteSession, positions: TenderPositions, qa: QaRecords, complete: bool, scenario: datetime,
            started: float, on_facts) -> TenderFacts | None:
    if not positions.positions and not _has_records(qa):
        session.trace.event(session.name, "tender_failed")
        return None
    if not positions.positions:
        session.trace.event(session.name, "tender_qa_only", note="no positions on this website; its Q&A is kept")
    facts = resolve_tender(positions.positions, qa, scenario, positions.number_format or None)
    facts.qa_complete = complete
    facts.seconds = round(time.monotonic() - started, 1)
    session.trace.event(session.name, "tender_facts", seconds=facts.seconds, qa_complete=complete,
                        amendments=[_amendment_text(a) for a in facts.amendments],
                        positions=[p.model_dump(mode="json") for p in facts.positions], problems=facts.problems)
    if on_facts is not None:
        on_facts(facts)
    return facts


async def _research_tender_one(session: SiteSession, reference: str, scenario: datetime, *,
                               deadline: float | None = None, on_facts=None) -> TenderFacts | None:
    """Positions and Q&A by one worker in one tab."""
    started = time.monotonic()
    collected = Collected()
    documents: list[str] = []
    output, _ = await run_worker(session, _goal(reference), Summary, deadline=deadline,
                                 max_steps=steps_for(20, deadline), thinking=False, grounded=False,
                                 tools=(paging_tool(collected, thorough=True), keep_tool(documents)))
    if not documents:  # the worker read the documents in its own tab instead
        documents = [session.seen]
    complete = collected.finished or (output is not None and not collected.pages)
    positions, qa = await asyncio.gather(read_positions("\n\n".join(documents), reference),
                                         read_qa(collected.reading(session.seen), reference))
    return _finish(session, positions, qa, complete, scenario, started, on_facts)


def merge_qa(base: QaRecords, extra: QaRecords) -> QaRecords:
    """
    `base` plus the records of `extra` whose answers base does not hold yet, per record kind: another website's
    answers, or answers a first read missed. An answer base already read keeps base's reading.
    """
    merged = base.model_copy(deep=True)
    merged.number_format = base.number_format or extra.number_format
    for name in QaRecords.model_fields:
        if name == "number_format":
            continue
        mine = list(getattr(merged, name))
        known = {norm_id(r.answer_number) for r in mine}
        mine += [r for r in getattr(extra, name) if norm_id(r.answer_number) not in known]
        setattr(merged, name, mine)
    return merged


def _record_count(qa: QaRecords) -> int:
    return sum(len(getattr(qa, name)) for name in QaRecords.model_fields if name != "number_format")


def combine(reads: list[TenderFacts], scenario: datetime) -> TenderFacts | None:
    """
    Several tender reads as one (positions on one website and Q&A on another, a retry, a targeted re-check):
    the positions of the read with the most of them, the Q&A answers of all reads (merge_qa, earlier reads
    first), resolved again by the same rules. None without reads.
    """
    if not reads:
        return None
    if len(reads) == 1:
        return reads[0]
    source = max(reads, key=lambda r: len(r.raw_positions))  # the first of equals
    qa = QaRecords()
    # the most complete read first: its reading of an answer wins over a partial read's; answers only another

def merge_qa(base: QaRecords, extra: QaRecords) -> QaRecords:
    """

    answers, or answers a first read missed. An answer base already read keeps base's reading.
    """
    merged = base.model_copy(deep=True)
    merged.number_format = base.number_format or extra.number_format
    for name in QaRecords.model_fields:
        if name == "number_format":
            continue
        mine = list(getattr(merged, name))
        known = {norm_id(r.answer_number) for r in mine}
        mine += [r for r in getattr(extra, name) if norm_id(r.answer_number) not in known]
        setattr(merged, name, mine)
    return merged

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

def qa_page(number: int, *answers: str, next_page: int | None = None, frame_loading: bool = False) -> str:
    """A list page as the extractor writes it: the outer page with the list in an embedded frame."""
    head = "Portal\n# Tender T-1\n[e1 link \"Back\" -> /]\n[frame /t/T-1/qa-frame]\n# Questions\n"
    if frame_loading:
        return head + "[frame /t/T-1/qa-list (separate)]\nFooter\n[/frame]\n[e2 link \"Ask\" -> /ask]\n"
    body = "".join(f"[img: {a}] | [e{3 + i} button \"Received\"] (tooltip: 2030-02-0{i + 1}T08:00:00Z) |\n"
                   f"- Answer {a} text\n|\n" for i, a in enumerate(answers))
    nav = f"Page {number}\n" + (f"[e9 link \"Next page\" -> /t/T-1/qa-list?page={next_page}]\n" if next_page else "")
    return head + "[frame /t/T-1/qa-list]\n" + body + nav + "[/frame]\nFooter\n[/frame]\n"
def standalone(number: int, *answers: str, next_page: int | None = None) -> str:
    """The same list page opened on its own (no outer page)."""
    body = "".join(f"[img: {a}] | [e{1 + i} button \"Received\"] (tooltip: 2030-02-0{i + 1}T08:00:00Z) |\n"
                   f"- Answer {a} text\n|\n" for i, a in enumerate(answers))
    nav = f"Page {number}\n" + (f"[e8 link \"Next page\" -> /t/T-1/qa-list?page={next_page}]\n" if next_page else "")
    return body + nav
class FakeSession:
    """Clicking the list's next control shows the next scripted view."""
    def __init__(self, views: list[str]):
        self.views, self.view, self.seen = views[1:], views[0], views[0]
        self.page = SimpleNamespace(url="https://tender.example.com/t/T-1?tab=qa", frames=[])
        self.trace, self.name = Events(), "tender:qa"
    async def act(self, kind, ref, fn):
        if self.views:
            self.view = self.views.pop(0)
            self.seen += "\n" + self.view
        return self.view
    async def look(self, *args, **kwargs):
        return self.view
def run(coro):
    return asyncio.run(coro)

def qa_page(number: int, *answers: str, next_page: int | None = None, frame_loading: bool = False) -> str:
    """A list page as the extractor writes it: the outer page with the list in an embedded frame."""
    head = "Portal\n# Tender T-1\n[e1 link \"Back\" -> /]\n[frame /t/T-1/qa-frame]\n# Questions\n"
    if frame_loading:
        return head + "[frame /t/T-1/qa-list (separate)]\nFooter\n[/frame]\n[e2 link \"Ask\" -> /ask]\n"
    body = "".join(f"[img: {a}] | [e{3 + i} button \"Received\"] (tooltip: 2030-02-0{i + 1}T08:00:00Z) |\n"
                   f"- Answer {a} text\n|\n" for i, a in enumerate(answers))
    nav = f"Page {number}\n" + (f"[e9 link \"Next page\" -> /t/T-1/qa-list?page={next_page}]\n" if next_page else "")
    return head + "[frame /t/T-1/qa-list]\n" + body + nav + "[/frame]\nFooter\n[/frame]\n"
def standalone(number: int, *answers: str, next_page: int | None = None) -> str:
    """The same list page opened on its own (no outer page)."""
    body = "".join(f"[img: {a}] | [e{1 + i} button \"Received\"] (tooltip: 2030-02-0{i + 1}T08:00:00Z) |\n"
                   f"- Answer {a} text\n|\n" for i, a in enumerate(answers))
    nav = f"Page {number}\n" + (f"[e8 link \"Next page\" -> /t/T-1/qa-list?page={next_page}]\n" if next_page else "")
    return body + nav
class FakeSession:
    """Clicking the list's next control shows the next scripted view."""
    def __init__(self, views: list[str]):
        self.views, self.view, self.seen = views[1:], views[0], views[0]
        self.page = SimpleNamespace(url="https://tender.example.com/t/T-1?tab=qa", frames=[])
        self.trace, self.name = Events(), "tender:qa"
    async def act(self, kind, ref, fn):
        if self.views:
            self.view = self.views.pop(0)
            self.seen += "\n" + self.view
        return self.view
    async def look(self, *args, **kwargs):
        return self.view
